cards.q: What is the final result of running the reducer across all elements of an array with reduce()?
In Array.prototype.reduce(), what is the "reducer"?
cards.a: A user-supplied callback function executed on each element of the array, in order.

cards.q: What does the accumulator parameter of a reduce() callback hold?
cards.a: The value resulting from the previous call to callbackFn.

cards.q: In a reduce() callback, what does the currentValue parameter hold?
cards.a: The value of the current element.

cards.q: What does the array argument passed to a reduce() callback refer to?
cards.a: The array reduce() was called upon.

cards.q: What are the two syntax forms of Array.prototype.reduce()?
Is the initialValue parameter of reduce() required or optional?
How is reduce() classified among Array methods?
What is passed into each reduce() callback invocation from the preceding element?
cards.a: The return value from the calculation on the preceding element.

cards.q: On the first reduce() callback call, what is accumulator when initialValue is specified?
On the first reduce() callback call, what is accumulator when initialValue is omitted?
When initialValue is omitted, from which index does reduce() iteration start?
On the first reduce() callback call, what is currentValue if initialValue is specified?
On the first reduce() callback call, what is currentValue if initialValue is not specified?
In what order does reduce() run the callback over array elements?
For which array slots is the reduce() callback not invoked?
cards.a: Empty slots in sparse arrays; it is invoked only for indexes with assigned values.

cards.q: What becomes the return value of reduce() after the final callback invocation?
cards.a: The final value of accumulator, returned by callbackFn on the last iteration.

Which argument accepted by other iterative array methods does reduce() not accept?
cards.a: thisArg; callbackFn is always called with undefined as this.
